beats.text: Orbit isn't about going up. It's about going sideways.
A ball thrown up just comes back down.
Throw it sideways harder and it lands farther.
Fast enough and the Earth curves away as fast as it falls. That's an orbit.
So rockets climb out of the air then tip sideways.
Nine tenths of a rocket's weight is fuel.
Empty tanks drop off so the rest speeds up.
Engines off, it falls around Earth every ninety minutes.
Follow for more, and see how everything works.
